title: Rights and Responsibilities of Consumers

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: Answer in one word: (a) What is the movement to protect consumer interests called? (b) Who can file a complaint in a consumer court?
questions.answer:
(a) Consumerism
(b) A consumer (also a registered consumer association or the government)

questions.q: Kavita bought a medicine without the date of manufacture and date of expiry printed on the package. (a) Which right is violated? (b) What should she have checked?
questions.answer:
(a) Right to be informed.
(b) The dates of manufacture and expiry, MRP and batch number before buying.

questions.q: Mr. Rajeev was crippled for life because of a doctor's negligence during treatment. (a) Which consumer right was violated? (b) What can he do?
questions.answer:
(a) Right to safety.
(b) Exercise his right to seek redressal — file a complaint for compensation in the consumer commission.

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) A consumer's responsibility includes proper use of products and services. (b) A responsible consumer tries to protect his interest on his own.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) True

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Consumer awareness means making a consumer aware of his rights and liabilities. (b) A shopkeeper who buys a shirt for his own use is a consumer.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) True

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: As part of the right to consumer education, what should consumers expect to be educated about?
questions.answer:
(1) The laws that prevent unfair trade practices.
(2) The ways dishonest traders deceive consumers.
(3) How to protect their own interests.
(4) The procedure for filing complaints.

questions.q: What is meant by the right to safety? Explain with an example.
questions.answer: The right to be protected against goods and services that are hazardous to life and health. Example: if a gas cylinder supplied leaks and causes a fire, the supplier is liable to pay compensation.

questions.q: State any two responsibilities of consumers.
questions.answer:
(1) Obtain proof of transaction — a cash memo or bill and warranty card.
(2) Make proper use of products and make only reasonable claims.
(Also self-help, awareness of rights.)

questions.q: What is meant by the right to choose?
questions.answer: Every consumer has the right to choose the goods he needs from a variety of similar products at competitive prices, without pressure from sellers or advertisements.

questions.q: State the concept of consumerism.
questions.answer: Consumerism is a movement by consumers and consumer associations to protect consumers against unfair practices of producers and sellers, to make consumers aware of their rights and responsibilities, and to ensure fair and honest dealings.

questions.q: Define consumer education with an example. OR Define proof of transaction with an example.
questions.answer:
Consumer education means making consumers aware of their rights, of market malpractices and of how to complain — e.g. the 'Jago Grahak Jago' campaign.
Proof of transaction is a document that proves a purchase — e.g. a cash memo, bill or warranty card, needed when making a claim.

questions.q: Who is a consumer?
questions.answer: A consumer is a person who buys goods or hires services for his own use, or for use by others on his behalf, and not for resale.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: How can consumers take care of their own interests and protect themselves from market malpractices — 'self-help is the best help'?
questions.answer:
(1) Collect information about products, prices and quality before buying.
(2) Check quality marks (ISI, AGMARK, hallmark), MRP, weight, dates of manufacture and expiry.
(3) Insist on a cash memo and warranty card, and keep them safely.
(4) Read labels and use products properly; be aware of rights and complain against cheating.

questions.q: What is meant by consumerism? Explain any one responsibility of consumers.
questions.answer:
Consumerism is a movement by consumers to ensure fair and honest practices by sellers and to protect themselves from exploitation.
Responsibility — proof of transaction: the consumer must always obtain and preserve the cash memo and warranty card, without which a claim for repair or replacement cannot be established.

questions.q: 'Every consumer must demand a proof of transaction such as a cash memo.' Identify the responsibility and explain it.
questions.answer: The responsibility to obtain proof of transaction. A bill, cash memo or warranty card proves the purchase, its date and price. If the goods turn out defective, the consumer can claim repair, replacement or compensation only on producing this proof.

questions.q: Explain the right to be heard and the right to seek redressal.
questions.answer:
Right to be heard: consumers' interests must receive due consideration — they are consulted in government policy, business listens to their views, and they are heard in consumer courts.
Right to seek redressal: consumers can get replacement, refund or compensation for defective goods, deficient services and unfair practices, through the seller or the consumer courts.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Who is a consumer? Explain the various responsibilities of a consumer.
questions.answer:
A consumer is a person who buys goods or services for his own use or for others on his behalf, not for resale.
(1) Self-help — be well informed and alert.
(2) Proof of transaction — obtain and keep cash memos and warranty cards.
(3) Proper claim — make only reasonable claims.
(4) Proper use of products — do not misuse goods under guarantee.
(5) Awareness of rights, checking quality marks and MRP, honouring agreements and timely payment, avoiding pirated goods.

questions.q: Describe briefly the right to safety, the right to be informed and the right to choose.
questions.answer:
Right to safety: protection against goods and services that endanger life or health — the seller is liable for injury from a defective product.
Right to be informed: to know the quality, quantity, purity, standard, price and expiry date of goods and the precautions in using them.
Right to choose: to select freely from a variety of goods at competitive prices without pressure from sellers.

questions.q: Describe briefly the responsibilities of a consumer.
questions.answer: Self-help; obtaining proof of transaction; making proper claims; proper use of products; being aware of rights; checking quality marks, weight and price; honouring agreements; not buying spurious or pirated goods; complaining against unfair practices.

questions.q: What is meant by consumerism? Explain any two responsibilities of a consumer.
questions.answer:
Consumerism is a movement by consumers and their associations to protect consumers from unfair and dishonest practices and to create awareness of their rights.
(1) Self-help — an informed consumer protects himself better than anyone else.
(2) Proper use of products and reasonable claims — misuse or exaggerated claims are irresponsible.
